results.question: Which country takes the largest share of Sri Lanka's tea exports?
results.answer: Iraq takes the largest share of Sri Lanka's tea exports, accounting for 10.9% of the total export value in 2024, which amounted to USD 149,621,564 out of USD 1,373,467,019 [3]. Sri Lanka exported tea to 145 destination markets in the same year, indicating a diversified market presence with a Herfindahl concentration index of 0.05 [4]. The United Arab Emirates was the fastest-growing destination for Sri Lankan tea between 2020 and 2024, with an annual growth rate of 31.6% [5]. There is no available data on the annual export volume of Sri Lanka's tea, as the Sri Lanka Tea Board's dataset contains no usable annual observations [1].

results.question: How fast have cinnamon exports grown over the last five years?
results.answer: Cinnamon exports from Sri Lanka have contracted at a rate of 0.2% per year over the last five years, reaching a total export value of USD 214,425,881 in 2024 [5]. Mexico was the largest market, accounting for 38.4% of the export value, while Honduras was the fastest-growing destination with a growth rate of 7.7% per year during this period [3][6]. Although there is no district-level production data available, the export figures provide a clear picture of the overall trend in cinnamon exports [1][2].

results.question: How concentrated are Sri Lanka's rubber export destinations?
results.answer: In 2024, Sri Lanka exported rubber to 36 different markets, with a total export value of USD 25,787,076 [3]. The largest single market was Pakistan, which accounted for 18.6% of the total export value, amounting to USD 4,797,272 [3]. The Herfindahl concentration index for these exports was 0.11, indicating a diversified export destination structure [4]. India was the fastest-growing destination for Sri Lankan rubber exports, with a compound annual growth rate of 18.1% from 2020 to 2024 [5]. However, no sourced export volume series is available for rubber, so information on volume concentration cannot be provided [1].

results.question: Which district contributes the largest share of cinnamon production?
results.answer: It is not possible to determine which district contributes the largest share of cinnamon production in Sri Lanka, as there is no recorded data on cinnamon-producing districts or their production shares [1][2]. results.question: Which markets buy the most Sri Lankan knitted apparel?
results.answer: In 2024, the United States was the largest market for Sri Lankan knitted apparel, purchasing USD 1,101,173,031, which accounted for 38.8% of the total export value of USD 2,838,863,126 [1]. Sri Lanka exported knitted apparel to 128 different markets, indicating a moderately concentrated market with a Herfindahl concentration index of 0.19 [2]. Over the period from 2020 to 2024, the export value of knitted apparel grew at a compound annual growth rate of 2.8% [3]. Croatia was the fastest-growing market for Sri Lankan knitted apparel during this period, with an annual growth rate of 41.9% [4]. The analysis is based on the HS-code category for knitted apparel, and data for the broader apparel category, including woven garments, could not be covered due to the absence of EDB Apparel sub-category data.
